subject: Post-call: RAG evaluation kit & model recommendations — NovusCare
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Varga <elena@novuscare.com>, Chris Taylor <chris.taylor@novuscare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: RAG evaluation kit & model recommendations — NovusCare

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum. Short version: NovusCare is a good fit for a focused RAG pilot in December. We covered retrieval topology, grounding risk tolerance, and acceptable latency envelope (~300-600ms p95 for chat flows).

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: accurate, source-grounded answers for internal clinical SOP documents + policies. Tolerance for minor hallucination is low; recall of the single best supporting doc (P@1) is top priority.
- Volume: expected steady-state 40k queries/mo, peak bursts up to ~250 qps during daytime.
- Deployment preference: hosted/Dedicated hybrid (initial pilot on hosted, Dedicated for production).

Recommended evaluation kit (what we'll run during the pilot):
1) Models to bench (generation + instruction):
   - rw-instruct-7b-q8 (low-latency baseline, quantized)
   - llama2-chat-13b-4k (high-quality reference)
   - mistral-instruct-8k (balanced quality/cost)
2) Retrieval settings to test:
   - dense-only (SBERT dense embedder) with chunk size 250 tokens, top_k=20
   - hybrid (BM25 + dense) with reranker downstream, chunk size 300, recall target top_10
   - document-level vs chunk-level tradeoff notes included in the attached eval-benchmarks.csv
3) Reranker options:
   - cross-encoder reranker (best precision@1, higher latency)
   - lightweight bi-encoder re-scoring (faster, lower single-best precision)
4) Grounding metrics we'll track:
   - Precision@1 (is the top answer supported by a document?)
   - Grounding Recall@5 (are supporting docs in top 5?)
   - Hallucination rate per 1k queries (manual label spot-check)

Artifacts we will share (attachments + Drive):
- prompt-set-v1.md (30 real-ish prompts tuned to your FAQ/SOP flows)
- eval-benchmarks.csv (expected vs. measured metrics placeholders; please replace with your sample docs)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bEvalKit-NovusCare (put your 150–200 sample docs there)

Asks/actions (next week):
- NovusCare: upload a 150–200 doc sample into the Drive folder by EOD Wed (Dec 2). If you have a redacted export, that’s fine.
- NovusCare: indicate whether Dedicated is a hard requirement for pilot go/no-go (helps scope Dedicated sizing).
- Redwood: run the initial retrieval + reranker sweep and return a short report (2–3 days after sample is uploaded).

Ben — can you scope the reranker latency estimates and add a note about caching primitives (KV/prefix cache) that will keep chat latencies inside their envelope? Rishi — will you queue the model variants for the bench runs?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval-benchmarks.csv, prompt-set-v1.md

Elena — quick answers and sizing notes below. TL;DR: cross-encoder reranker is viable for your p95 target if we combine it with a fast first-stage retriever + caching; Dedicated helps for steady-state throughput.

Reranker performance tradeoffs:
- Cross-encoder (recommended for initial pilot to maximize P@1): expect additional 70–180ms per query for a medium-sized cross-encoder (depends on batch size and GPU). If we run a quantized x-encoder on a V100/A10-class GPU with batching, p95 overhead is ~120ms.
- Bi-encoder/fast re-score: <30ms overhead but P@1 drops ~6–10% in our internal benchmarks. Good fallback when strict latency SLAs apply.

Topology recs to hit p95 < 600ms: 
1) First-stage dense retrieval with top_k=50 (local ANN like FAISS/IVF) -> 10–20ms
2) Lightweight re-score (optional) -> +20ms
3) Cross-encoder rerank on top_10 -> +120ms (with batching and GPU affinity)
4) Generation step (rw-instruct-7b-q8) -> 200–300ms depending on length and streaming
5) With prefix/KV caching for short chats, we've measured overall p95 in pilot configs ~450–550ms.

Dedicated sizing / cost pointers: we can size a 2x A10 pool to handle 250 qps peak with autoscale headroom. I’ll add a conservative MRR estimate in HubSpot (DEAL-00942) and follow up with a more detailed quote.

Security note: for SOC2/PII docs, recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS + audit logs. We can provide our data handling checklist for legal/security.

I attached a short latency estimate sheet (reranker-latency-estimates.pdf) and added a link to our public RAG playbook.

—Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
